title: English: stories from yesterday
description: Build clear past-tense sentences about finished events.
subject: English
objectives: Use regular and common irregular past forms
Use did with the base form in questions and negatives
Choose was or were and recognize finished past time

sources.title: English: stories from yesterday · Original study notes
sources.text:
Use the simple past to describe completed events at a finished past time. Expressions such as yesterday, last Saturday, and two days ago often identify that time. For example, “I visited a park yesterday” describes a completed visit.
Many verbs are regular: add -ed to form the past, as in play → played and walk → walked. If the verb already ends in e, add d, as in live → lived. Some verbs are irregular and need a different form: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw, and have → had. In affirmative simple-past sentences, these forms are the same for I, you, he, she, we, and they: “She went” and “They went.”
For most verbs, a negative uses did not (didn't) followed by the base form: “He did not play.” A question uses Did + subject + base form: “Did they go?” Did already marks the past, so do not write “didn't played” or “Did they went?”
The verb be has its own simple-past forms. Use was with I, he, she, and it; use were with you, we, and they. Examples: “I was tired” and “They were at home.” For negatives use was not or were not. For questions move was or were before the subject: “Were you tired?” Do not add did to these basic be sentences.
Time clues help, but the meaning matters too. “Every day” often describes a routine, while “yesterday” identifies a finished past time. In a sentence such as “Yesterday, we walked home,” both the time expression and verb form match a completed past event. These notes focus on the simple past; they do not cover every possible use of past forms.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about yesterday.
questions.explanation: Play is regular. Add -ed to describe the completed event: played.

lesson.title: Regular past forms
steps: Find the completed past time: yesterday.
For the regular verb play, add -ed: played.
lesson.takeaway: For the regular verb play, add -ed: played.

practice.prompt: Complete: “Last Saturday, we ___ to the shop.”
practice.explanation: Walk is a regular verb; its past form is walked.

questions.prompt: Complete: “She ___ to the library two days ago.”
questions.explanation: Go has the irregular past form went. Do not add -ed to make goed.

lesson.title: Irregular past forms
steps: Some verbs do not form the past with -ed.
Learn the pair go → went, then use went with any subject in an affirmative past sentence.
lesson.takeaway: Learn the pair go → went, then use went with any subject in an affirmative past sentence.

practice.explanation: Eat has the irregular past form ate.

questions.explanation: Use did not + base form. Did marks the past, so play stays in its base form.

lesson.title: Past negatives
steps: Add did not to mark a past negative.
Use the base verb play, not played.
lesson.takeaway: Use the base verb play, not played.

practice.explanation: After did not, use the base form go.

questions.explanation: A simple-past question usually uses Did + subject + base form: Did they visit...?

lesson.title: Past questions
steps: Follow the subject with the base form visit.
Do not mark the verb as past again after did.
lesson.takeaway: Do not mark the verb as past again after did.

practice.explanation: Use Did + she + see. See is the base form of saw.

questions.prompt: Complete: “I ___ tired, but my friends ___ excited.”
questions.explanation: Use was with I and were with the plural subject my friends.

lesson.title: Was and were
steps: Use was with I, he, she, and it.
Use were with you, we, and they or plural subjects.
lesson.takeaway: Use were with you, we, and they or plural subjects.

practice.prompt: Complete: “You ___ at home, and she ___ at school.”
practice.explanation: You takes were; she takes was.

questions.prompt: Which expression most clearly identifies a finished past time in “We visited the garden ___”?
questions.explanation: Yesterday identifies a completed past time and matches visited. Next week and tomorrow refer to future time.

lesson.title: Finished past time
steps: Look at the verb visited: it describes a past visit.
Choose a time expression that refers to a finished past time.

practice.prompt: Which sentence clearly describes a completed past event?
practice.explanation: Walked and last Sunday both identify a completed past event.
